data.content_ref: inline:SRC_002's absolute claim ('always more resilient') is refuted by its own counterexample logic: if a decentralized network uses economic incentives or deliberate governance to force dependency diversity, the emergent homogeneity assumption fails. The target even lists this as a countercondition, yet maintains the universal claim. A large service can also have a single catastrophic correlated failure (e.g., a shared control plane or a monocultural internal tool) that takes down all strictly-more-redundant units simultaneously; 'strictly more total internal redundancy' does not guarantee more resilience if that redundancy is nullified by a common-mode failure. Thus the strong universal quantifier is unjustified.
